transcript.text: I can certainly help with that. The most common reason a washing machine won't spin is that it hasn't finished draining the water first; the machine will refuse to spin if there's still water in the drum. This is often caused by a blockage in the pump filter or a fault with the drain pump itself. To narrow this down, could you please check: Is there still water in the drum, or has it drained completely?
no water in the drum, its drained fine. just the wet mat left in there

The next most common reason for this is an unbalanced load; if you had just one heavy item like a bath mat or rug in there, the machine will often refuse to spin because it cannot balance itself. Could you tell me exactly what was in the drum when it failed? If it was just that single item, try adding a few towels or other clothes to balance the load and run a spin-only cycle again.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
it was just the big rubber backed bath mat on its own, its dirty from the dog. ill try it with a couple of towels

That is exactly the right approach. A single heavy rubber-backed mat often sticks to one side and prevents the machine from spinning because it cannot balance itself; adding a few towels helps distribute the weight evenly. Please run that spin cycle now and let me know if it works or if it still refuses to spin. If it does work, we can look at how you wash mats in future (perhaps washing them with some other items). If it still won't spin even when empty, I'll need your make and model number to check the drive system.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
ok did the rinse & spin with the mat and a couple of towels, it spun up fine and the mat came out damp not dripping. so was it just the mat?

Yes, exactly. A single rubber-backed bath mat is a classic cause for this because it soaks up water and sticks to one side of the drum. The machine’s sensors detected that imbalance and refused to spin at high speed to prevent damage or walking. Adding towels helped balance the weight, which allowed it to spin normally. To avoid this in future, try washing heavy mats with a few lighter items like towels to keep things balanced. If you ever need help with anything else, just let me know.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
